author: Sangmin Kim
title: 2 men face up to 19 years for transporting meth in Kern County - NewsBreak
text:
By Sangmin Kim ,
10 hours ago
BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (KGET) — Two men were found guilty Monday of transporting about 50 pounds of methamphetamine for sale, according to the Kern County District Attorney’s Office.
A Kern County jury found Ismael Gonzalez Jr., 34, and David Mendoza, 31, each guilty of possession for sale of a controlled substance, transportation for sale of a controlled substance and conspiracy, the DA’s office said in a press release.
Watch ‘After Sunrise’ on KGET+; Click to learn how to get KGET+ on your smart TV devices The jury also found Gonzalez and Mendoza possessed methamphetamine that exceeded 20 kilograms.
The sentencing hearing is set for May 28, where Gonzalez and Mendoza are facing up to 19 years in prison, according to prosecutors.
“Illegal substances are often catalysts for severe violence and devastation within our communities,” District Attorney Cynthia Zimmer said in the press release.
“Holding accountable those who distribute and transport them, especially in such large quantities, is a critical step toward reducing that damage. The scale of drugs involved in this case is significant and under the law, warrants substantial penalties.”
At around 4 p.m. Jan. 5, Kern County sheriff’s deputies performed a traffic stop on their vehicle traveling south on Interstate 5 near Lebec.
The stop was conducted after officials noticed the vehicle had an illegal window tint and an invalid license plate. The vehicle also made an illegal lane change, officials said.
A search of the vehicle led to deputies finding about 50 pounds of methamphetamine, according to prosecutors.
